text:
Maya: Uploaded a new compact onboarding variant in Figma. Key idea: mini sample card strip that expands inline instead of the sticky bottom bar. Link: https://www.figma.com/file/abc123 (frame 'Onboard / Mini Strip'). Feedback?

Dan: Nice. Feels lighter. My immediate worry is low discoverability on small screens if the strip is collapsed by default. How will users notice it?

Jess: Suggest we test two cohorts: default-expanded vs collapsed-with-pill. Metric: %who-start-sample within first session and time-to-first-api-key. 5k users each should be enough for signal.

Priya: Accessibility notes from quick scan: contrast of the pill label is 3.8:1 in the mock, needs >=4.5:1. Also the focus outline is only 1px; recommend a stronger visible focus (2-3px solid or accessible shadow).

Sam: Implementation heads-up: if we keep the pill toggle, ensure DOM order respects keyboard flow. Current mock puts toggle after the card content which makes tab order awkward. Move the toggle to be first interactive element in the region or add tabindex=0 appropriately.

Rina: UX microcopy — what short label for the CTA? Options: "Try sample", "Create demo project", "Start with sample". Mobile width matters: "Try sample" is the shortest.

Jess: "Try sample" feels informal but low friction. For enterprise flows maybe prefer "Create sample project" to be explicit. We can surface an org-level override for copy.

Maya: Agree on org override. Also thinking of a small "Why samples?" tooltip icon that briefly explains benefits (preseeded prompts, example pipelines). Would that clutter?

Dan: Tooltip is fine if hidden behind an icon. But make sure its accessible: aria-describedby with an id and keyboard focusable trigger.

Priya: VoiceOver note: when a sample is selected and the onboarding step advances, we should use aria-live="polite" on the step region so SR users get the update. Also ensure expanded/collapsed uses aria-expanded on the toggle and role="region" with an accessible label.

Sam: CSS snippet to keep touch targets sane on mobile:
```css
.onboard-pill { min-height: 44px; padding: 10px 14px; display: inline-flex; align-items: center; }
.mini-strip { overflow-x: auto; -webkit-overflow-scrolling: touch; }
```
This preserves a compact look but keeps 44px touch targets.

Maya: Good. Also: what's our plan for enterprise accounts where samples are noise? Can we default-off and let admins enable?

Jess: Propose a per-org setting: samples.default = true for self-serve orgs, false for managed enterprise. Also persist user-level preference so power users can opt out independent of org default.

Dan: Analytics: tag clicks with data-qa attributes, e.g., data-qa="onboard-sample-cta" and GA event category "onboarding" action "sample_click". Jess, can you add to the analytics checklist?

Jess: Yup. Will add events: sample_impression, sample_expand, sample_click, sample_complete. Will also track keyboard activation vs mouse.

a11y-bot: Auto-scan: missing aria-label on the collapse chevron in the mock. Recommend aria-label="Expand samples" / "Collapse samples". Also flag contrast on btn-text.

Priya: Also check color pair when overlay is active; ensure text overlaid on images maintains 4.5:1. And add visible focus for high-contrast mode.

Maya: I'll update Figma: 1) pill copy to "Try sample" for mobile, full label for desktop, 2) adjust colors to meet 4.5:1, 3) add a11y annotations (aria-live, aria-expanded, aria-labels), 4) add tooltip content. I'll post updated frames by tomorrow morning and include a short usability script (4-6 tasks) focusing on discovery + keyboard flow.

Sam: For the devs: I'll send a tiny PR that reorders DOM so toggle is first element in region and add data-qa attributes. Also wire Space/Enter activation and role=button for non-button elements.

Jess: Sounds good. I'll spin up the A/B in GA and coordinate with analytics to report sample conversion after 1 week.

Maya: Thanks team. Follow-up: once frames are updated, let's do a 10-min keyboard walkthrough together in #design-review and then finalize the enterprise default flag behavior.

Dan: :thumbsup:

Rina: Quick microcopy decision: add parenthetical "(recommended)" after the toggle label? It nudges PLG users but might annoy enterprise admins. Maybe visible only when default is ON.

Priya: If you include "(recommended)", don't hide it with sr-only — keep it visible and test readability. Also ensure it's localized-friendly (short).

Maya: Noted. Will include both variants in Figma notes. Thanks everyone!
